elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Retained §5.1(a): IBM "will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill ... the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature" — substantively a professional-manner warranty.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted §5.1(c): "the software portions of the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted §5.1(c) runs only "for ninety (90) days following delivery"; no 12-month period is granted.
Inserted §5.1(d) gives "thirty (30) days following their performance", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence: "at IBM's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services".
Same sentence: "or a refund of the charges paid for them".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained p0063: "IBM covenants that it will comply with the laws applicable to IBM's business." (a covenant rather than a warranty, and scoped to IBM's business, but it delivers the compliance-with-law undertaking).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears anywhere in §5.1 as rendered; the drafter expressly did not pursue it.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: New §5.1(c): "for ninety (90) days following delivery, the software portions of the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation" — 90 days, documentation-conformance, express software warranty.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: New §5.1(d): "the Services will conform to the warranty in Subsection 5.1(a) for thirty (30) days following their performance" — attaches a 30-day duration to the retained care-and-skill warranty.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in Subsections 5.1(c) and 5.1(d) is, at IBM's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services..."
"...or a refund of the charges paid for them" — refund limb present and tied to both new warranties.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, 30-day Services warranty, and an express repair/replacement-or-refund remedy are all in operative text inside §5.1, so §5.2's exclusivity clause carries them rather than excluding them.

Preferred level fails on three elements the drafter deliberately did not pursue: 12-month software period (only 90 days), 90-day Services period (only 30 days), and the no-malicious-code warranty (absent). To reach preferred, change "ninety (90) days" in 5.1(c) to twelve (12) months, "thirty (30) days" in 5.1(d) to ninety (90) days, and add a warranty that the Services and any deliverables will be free of viruses, malicious or disabling code.

Minimality holds: the redline is a pure insertion of subsections (c) and (d) plus one remedy sentence; nothing outside the checklist is deleted or added (no survival tail, no expense allocation, no extra damages categories), and the favourable retained 5.1(a) care-and-skill language and 5.1 compliance covenant are preserved and reused as the Services warranty standard.

Intent is preserved: §5.2 exclusivity, §5.4(a) no-error-free-operation and §5.4(c) AS IS for Materials/non-IBM items continue to operate without direct contradiction, since the new warranty is qualified "in all material respects" and 5.4(c) is confined to non-IBM items.

Advisory (not a defect at this level): if any "software portions of the Base Components" are third-party software, §5.4(c)'s AS IS disclaimer could be read to overlap the new §5.1(c). If the counterparty raises this, the narrowest cure is to add "Notwithstanding Section 5.4(c)," at the head of 5.1(c) rather than editing the disclaimer.

Confirm "Base Components" is a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement (it is not in the supplied definitions extract); if it is not defined, the inserted 5.1(c) would rest on an undefined term and should be re-anchored to the software provided by IBM as part of the Services.
